newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine business sees peso rebounding.
newsitem.headline: Philippine business sees peso rebounding.

text.p: Philippine businessmen expect the peso to rebound to near its level before its de facto devaluation last Friday, Philippine Chamber of Commerce and Industry president Federico Pascual said on Sunday.
"The final rate will not be far off from where we were before the sharp fall," Pascual told Reuters.
The peso hovered around 26.30-26.40 to the dollar in the weeks before the Central Bank allowed it to fluctuate within a wider range.
The peso quickly fell to its 45-month low of 29.45 before trading was suspended due to the wild fluctuation. Trading will resume on Monday.
Pascual said the sharp fall was engineered by speculators and was not backed by economic fundamentals.
The normal supply and demand forces would eventually put the peso in a equilibrium in the coming days, he said.
He said the robust export sector would provide the needed foreign exchange to shore up the peso's value.
Some other analysts forecast the peso to weaken to between 27.00 and 29.00 because of the country's trade deficit.
